blocks.text: Read the chapter with this setting in view: Greek and Latin Psalter traditions number many psalms differently from the Masoretic tradition because they combine Psalms 9-10 and 114-115, divide Psalms 116 and 147, and transmit Psalm 151 beyond the 150-psalm count. It gives a starting point for following the chapter's own movement. The chapter itself should determine how far the point is taken. The evidence leaves some details unresolved.

A literary feature to notice is that The Masoretic Psalter contains 150 psalms arranged in five books, with doxological boundaries after Psalms 41, 72, 89, and 106 and a final crescendo of praise in Psalms 146-150. This form helps organize the chapter's claims. Notice it before drawing broader conclusions from a single phrase or image. A more precise reconstruction remains disputed.
